question: Did Jesus tell his disciples everything?
summary: In John 15:15 Jesus declares he has made known to his disciples "all things" he heard from the Father — the word is *panta*, everything. One chapter later, in John 16:12, he tells them he still has many things to say to them that they cannot bear right now. Same discourse, same audience, two flatly opposed claims about how much Jesus has communicated.

reconcile.connective: Gill reads 'all things' in 15:15 as the gospel's core already delivered, and the 'many things' still withheld in 16:12 as later truths reserved for the Spirit.

discrepancy.connective: Raymond E. Brown reads John 15-17 as a later compositional layer whose 16:12 promise of ongoing Spirit-revelation comes at the cost of contradicting 15:15's 'all things' claim.

pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley gives this exact pairing its own two-column heading, 'Christ's revelation of truth, complete. / Much kept back by him,' quoting John 15:15 and John 16:12 verbatim side by side (Historical Discrepancies chapter, ~p. 330), and argues 15:15's 'all things' means everything the Father had, up to that time, designed for the disciples to know, while 16:12's 'many things' are the post-resurrection and Spirit-taught teaching still to come.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why did Jesus say, "I have called you friends" in John 15:15?
link.note: Explicitly reconciles 15:15's full disclosure with 16:12's 'cannot bear them' by distinguishing what Jesus revealed from the disciples' finite capacity to comprehend it at the time.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: I have yet many things to say unto you,.... Not with respect to the main doctrines of the Gospel, for everything of this kind he had made known unto them, Joh 15:15; but what regarded the rejection of the Jews, and the calling of the Gentiles, the abrogation of the Mosaic economy, and settling the Gospel church state, which were to come to pass after the death and resurrection of Christ, and the sending of the Spirit: but ye cannot bear them now; because of their prejudices in favour of their own nation, the law of Moses, and the ceremonies of it, and the setting up of a temporal kingdom.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's John 16:12 exposition is embedded (upstream scrape artifact — the paragraph is appended under the note_ref for 16:10, preceded by repeated 'joh 16:12' headers, which are trimmed as non-content) but explicitly cross-cites Joh 15:15 by verse number and states the resolving distinction: core gospel doctrine already disclosed vs. later redemptive-historical specifics (Gentile mission, end of Mosaic economy) reserved until after the resurrection. verse_ref is set to John 16:12 (what the quote is actually about) rather than the note's own mislabeled 'ref' field (John 16:10); full_note_ref preserves the source's literal note_ref for traceability.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. This is to be understood of the judiciary power and authority of Christ, who has "all judgment" committed to him by the Father, as Mediator; has all power in heaven and in earth; and as he is appointed, so he is a very fit person to judge the world at the last day. Now this being disputed and disbelieved by the Jews, the Holy Ghost, in the ministry of Peter, most clearly demonstrated to their full conviction, that he was raised from the dead, set upon his throne, and was made, or declared, Lord and Christ, Act 2:24; of which the pouring forth of the Holy Ghost was an evidence; and the instance in the text proving it, and which is a very considerable one, is the judgment, or condemnation and destruction of Satan, the prince of the world; for Christ, by his death, has destroyed him and his works; has spoiled his principalities and powers; and by his resurrection from the dead, and ascension to heaven, has carried him and them captive, triumphing over them; and, through the effusion of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, and the power of it attending their ministry, Satan was judged, condemned, and cast out of the Heathen world, their temples, and the souls of men; the prey was taken from the mighty, and the lawful captive delivered: but as this may refer to the ordinary work of the Spirit in conviction and conversion, it may be differently applied; for he convinces of various things, which come under this name: he convinces of the wrong judgment which men in a state of nature form of God, whom they take to be such an one as themselves; of a crucified Christ, whom they esteem foolishness; of the doctrines of Christ, which they judge to be absurd and irrational; of the people of Christ, whom they reckon the filth of the world, and the offscouring of all things; of the ways and, ordinances of Christ, which are thought to be grievous, unpleasant, and unprofitable; and of themselves, and their own state and condition, which they fancy to be good, and they in a fair way for heaven: he also convinces them of the excellency, truth, power, and usefulness of the Gospel, which is called "judgment", Isa 42:1, so as to understand it truly, believe it cordially, receive it in the love of it, and feel the power of it: he convinces them of a future judgment; of the reality and certainty of it; that it will be universal, reach to all persons and things; that it will be carried on in the most righteous manner, and there will be no escaping it, of which the judgment and condemnation of Satan is a standing proof: and he moreover convinces of judgment or damnation; that men are under a sentence of condemnation in Adam; that they are liable to eternal damnation in themselves; that except they believe in Christ they will be damned, as sure as the prince of this world is.
